Apple today claimed that a new UK proposal over App Store fees amounts to price regulation, warning it could harm innovation and investment. Here's the full story.

Apple fights back against UK App Store regulation

According to Reuters, Apple today submitted a formal response to a consultation from the UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), opposing a proposed rule that would allow app developers to link to alternative payment methods.

The CMA can impose such requirements after designating Apple and Google as having "strategic market status" in their respective mobile platform markets last year. Under the UK's new digital markets regime, that designation gives the regulator the power to introduce company-specific rules to foster competition and give consumers more choice.

Under the proposal, Apple and Google could still charge a commission on transactions completed via alternative payment methods, but any related fees would have to be considered "fair and reasonable".

Reuters noted that the CMA "expects that the resulting fees will be lower than current app store charges, with savings passed on to UK consumers, or reinvested in developers' businesses to support innovation".

Apple, however, sees things differently, and is opposing the proposal. Here's Reuters' report:

而

The CMA has rejected Apple's characterisation of the proposal as price regulation, saying it intends to set principles for judging whether steering fees are fair and reasonable, rather than dictating the level of fees directly.
